description: Separate SELF from WORLD from BOARD (the agent's design's decomposition; the core skill real-camera play needs). The eye's respond_votes credits anything that CHANGES, so it cannot tell the controlled avatar from an autonomous drifter (both move every frame). The discriminator is the agent's own: CONTROLLABLE = motion that FOLLOWS my commands — its velocity CHANGES when I change action (high velocity-variability under my varied exploration); AUTONOMOUS = motion INDEPENDENT of my action (constant velocity regardless of what I press → near-zero velocity-variability but nonzero speed); INVARIANT = never moves. velocity-variability is tracked by folding the frame-to-frame change of [drow,dcol] (the closed loop). (This is the tractable proxy on a constant-velocity world; the fully general form is per-region action-correlation / per-action response variance.)

microtheory.name: nd_self_world
microtheory.description: self = velocity follows my commands (high vel-variability under exploration); world = constant velocity, action-independent; board = still.

rules.name: track_velocity_variability
rules.comment: Fold the frame-to-frame change of the region's velocity into velvar (EMA). drow_prev/dcol_prev are the last frame's velocity (committed at the clock edge); velvar accumulates |drow-drow_prev|+|dcol-dcol_prev|. A region whose velocity tracks my varied actions has high velvar; a constant-velocity drifter ~0. clocked=1 so the engine folds next_*->*.

rules.name: classify_axis
rules.comment: Classify each region from how it behaves under my exploration: INVARIANT if it has not moved (max speed seen ~0); else CONTROLLABLE if its velocity-variability is high (it follows my commands) or AUTONOMOUS if low (constant velocity, action-independent). Sets axis_kind. Uses ever_speed (max squared speed seen) so a region that has ever moved is not called invariant on a still frame.
